answer: Israel's 120-seat Knesset is elected by proportional vote in one national district, with a 3.25% threshold. No party has ever won a majority, so every government is a coalition and small parties have leverage. In November 2022, by the Central Elections Committee's results, Likud won 32 seats and Yesh Atid 24; a Likud-led government took office in December 2022, with guidelines declaring the Jewish people's "exclusive and indisputable right" to all parts of the Land of Israel. The parties differ: the Israel Democracy Institute says Hadash was among the first to champion two states for two peoples, and Religious Zionism advocates the "Greater Land of Israel". Ra'am joined the 2021 Bennett-Lapid coalition, the first time an Arab party was a formal coalition member. After the October 2026 election, Reuters reports, neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot had a clear path to a majority.

Positions of National Unity and Noam on a Palestinian state; National Unity's seat total after the 2023 split; seat counts after splits during the 2022 to 2026 term.

not_claimed: That any party speaks for a whole community: Arab citizens, ultra-Orthodox, secular, settlers and others vote across many lists.
That the camps are monoliths or that a party's platform equals its voters' views.
That one camp is more legitimate than another.
That describing a party's roots means every member shares the founders' positions.

answer_claims.says: Israel's 120-seat Knesset is elected by proportional vote in one national district, with a 3.25% threshold.
No party has ever won a majority, so every government is a coalition and small parties have leverage.

A Likud-led government took office in December 2022, with guidelines declaring the Jewish people's "exclusive and indisputable right" to all parts of the Land of Israel.
The parties differ: the Israel Democracy Institute says Hadash was among the first to champion two states for two peoples, and Religious Zionism advocates the "Greater Land of Israel".
Ra'am joined the 2021 Bennett-Lapid coalition, the first time an Arab party was a formal coalition member.
After the October 2026 election, Reuters reports, neither Netanyahu nor Eisenkot had a clear path to a majority.

skeptic.notes: Checked seats and votes against votes25.bechirot.gov.il and votes26.bechirot.gov.il (fetched): all 2022 and 2026 figures in facts 2, 3, 10 match; 2026 seats sum to 120; 27+6+7+6+7 = 53 recomputed. Reuters' graphic on the same page independently reports 53 seats for its 'Netanyahu-led bloc' and 48 for Eisenkot's bloc, so the grouping is not only ours; the card now says whose grouping the 53 is. Read the IDI, Haaretz, INN, Freedom House, UN News, JPost, Britannica, JVL, CFR, Anadolu and IFES pages. must-fix: fact 11 cited the Guardian for 'roots in Kach', but the cited Guardian passage (and the piece) does not say that of Otzma Yehudit; source and claim removed. The fact now has the IDI and Reuters (wire) only. must-fix: facts 8, 9, 11, 13, 14, 16 have two reliable sources, not three: the IDI party pages are one site and nothing independent confirms them (the gate refuses). should-fix: the 1988 Kach disqualification is a court record (Supreme Court) that no source here opens; fact 12 rests on the IDI, the Guardian and Reuters via Ynetnews, with the amendment's date taken from the Guardian. The Times of Israel page for fact 6 could not be re-read online (kept from the lock). The 2022 guidelines are read only through INN, Freedom House and Just Security, not the Knesset text. Party descriptions: no characterisation in our voice; 'far right'/'far-right' appears only attributed (IDI, Haaretz) in contested and fact 9. Fact 13 omitted the IDI's own note that Shas voted hawkishly in the Knesset; added. Strongest objections: (Israeli political scientist) a seat list shows who won, not who 'speaks for' anyone; the card answers with institutions, not the claim, and does not report the share of voters outside the five-party grouping. (critic of a Jewish state) the card offers Ra'am as inclusion but Arab lists' seat counts and exclusion from coalitions are not set beside it; fact 16 gives Balad's 'state of all its citizens' platform but not the disqualification attempts, which no source here covers. Fixed by me: fact 3 wording (our arithmetic, our grouping), fact 11 (Guardian removed), fact 13 (IDI hawkish-votes clause).
